class_name: 話題-提示-トイウノハ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

glosses: as for; when it comes to
patterns.usage_note: Raises a clause or noun phrase as the topic and comments on it, typically with an evaluation or complaint (一人で引っ越しするってのは案外きつい, あいつの言い訳ってのは、いつも同じだ). The sibling lane uses the same shape to define a word, taking a bare noun and saying what it denotes (おやつってのは、食事の間に食べる軽い物だ). A plain-form verb or i-adjective clause can sit directly in front of it, where bare は would need のは.

examples.ruby: 毎朝[まいあさ]早[はや]く起[お]きるってのは、思[おも]ったより大変[たいへん]だ。
examples.english: Getting up early every morning is rougher than you'd expect.

examples.ruby: あいつの言[い]い訳[わけ]ってのは、いつも同[おな]じ話[はなし]だ。
examples.english: With that guy's excuses, it's always the exact same story.

examples.ruby: 一人[ひとり]で引[ひ]っ越[こ]しするってのは、案外[あんがい]きついよ。
examples.english: Moving house on your own is surprisingly brutal, let me tell you.

patterns.usage_note: Sets up an embedded question and answers it in the same breath: なぜ山に登るかというと、忘れられないからだ. With なぜ or どうして it is the standard way back into a reason, and the answer clause typically closes with ～からだ or ～ためだ. It also forms the concessive ～かというとそうでもない, conceding that the obvious answer is not quite right. Its sibling というと instead picks up a word already said.

examples.ruby: なぜ山[やま]に登[のぼ]るかというと、頂上[ちょうじょう]の風[かぜ]が忘[わす]れられないからだ。
examples.english: If you ask why I climb, it's because I can't forget the wind at the summit.

examples.ruby: 何[なに]が壊[こわ]れたかというと、洗濯機[せんたくき]のドアの部品[ぶひん]です。
examples.english: As for what broke, it's the little part on the washing machine door.

examples.ruby: 誰[だれ]が担当[たんとう]かというと、実[じつ]は私[わたし]なんです。
examples.english: As to who's in charge, it's actually me.
